name: Jira
description: Jira is Atlassian's project-management platform for planning, tracking, and delivering work across the software development lifecycle.
best_for: Positioned for teams working across the software development lifecycle who want to align work to goals and coordinate across engineering, product, and marketing.
features: Align work to goals across cross-functional teams
Break down projects into tasks with AI-powered assignment
Track work across boards, lists, timelines, and calendars
Automate workflows integrated with your existing tech stack

alternatives.name: Linear
alternatives.description: A product development system combining issue tracking, planning, and AI agent collaboration.
alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting a faster, more opinionated issue tracker

alternatives.name: Asana
alternatives.description: A work-management platform focused on projects, tasks, timelines, and team coordination.
alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting a more general-purpose work-management tool

alternatives.name: ClickUp
alternatives.description: A project-management platform with tasks, dashboards, documents, and workflow automation.
alternatives.best_for: Teams wanting an all-in-one workspace beyond issue tracking

alternatives.name: Zoho Projects
alternatives.description: An online project management platform for planning, tracking, and collaborating on work, with deep integration into the wider Zoho suite.
alternatives.best_for: Teams already using Zoho apps, and organizations wanting an affordable, feature-rich project tool

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Free forever for up to 10 users. Includes unlimited goals/projects/tasks/forms, 150 automation steps per subscription per month, 2 GB storage, community-only support. Billing basis: n/a.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: Verified on official pricing calculator at a team size of 1-11 users, monthly billing. This is a volume-tiered per-seat price: it drops to $7.91/user/month when the calculator is set to 300 users. Annual billing is sold in flat user-count bands rather than a simple per-seat rate, e.g. $900/year total for the '1-10 users' tier (any headcount 1-10 pays the same $900), $23,500/year for the '201-300' tier. 9/5 regional support, no uptime SLA.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.notes: Verified on official pricing calculator at 1-11 users, monthly billing; drops to $14.54/user/month at 300 users (same volume-tiering as Standard). Annual billing uses the same banded structure, e.g. $1,850/year for the '1-10 users' tier. Includes 99.9% uptime SLA and 24/7 support for critical issues.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: No public price. Billed annually only (not offered on monthly billing), and the pricing calculator only reveals an Enterprise line once you enter 801+ users; below that it just says to contact sales. 99.95% uptime SLA, 24/7 support for all issues.

cons: Per-seat price is not a fixed number but a volume-tiered rate that changes with the team-size figure you enter: on the official calculator, monthly billing shows Standard at $9.05/user/month and Premium at $18.30/user/month for a small team, but the same plans drop to $7.91 and $14.54 per user/month once the team size is set to 300 -- and annual billing is sold in discrete user-count bands (e.g. a flat $900/year covers any headcount from 1-10 users on Standard, $23,500/year covers any headcount from 201-300), so two teams of very different sizes within a band pay identically and crossing a band boundary jumps the whole invoice.

No uptime SLA and no 24/7 support until the Premium tier: the Free and Standard plans carry no guaranteed uptime SLA at all (per Atlassian's own comparison table), and Standard support is limited to '9/5 regional support' business hours -- 24/7 support (for critical issues) and the first SLA (99.9%) only start on Premium, with full 24/7 support on everything only at Enterprise (99.95% SLA).

Enterprise has zero public pricing and a self-serve barrier: it is billed annually only (no monthly option), sold exclusively through 'Contact sales,' and the online pricing calculator won't even surface an Enterprise price line unless you enter 801 or more users -- so there is no way to get a standard list price for an enterprise deployment without going through a sales conversation.
